positive-integer.name: positive integer
positive-integer.definition: A whole number greater than zero. It has no fractional part; zero and negative numbers are not positive integers.

integer.name: integer
integer.definition: A whole number with no fractional part. Integers may be negative, zero or positive; being an integer alone does not make a value a valid positive quantity.

safe-integer.name: safe integer
safe-integer.definition: An integer inside JavaScript Number's reliable integer range, from -9,007,199,254,740,991 through 9,007,199,254,740,991 inclusive. Adjacent integers in this range can be represented and distinguished exactly. This quantity contract additionally requires the integer to be positive.

finite-number.name: finite number
finite-number.definition: A JavaScript number that is neither NaN nor positive or negative Infinity. Finite numbers can have fractional parts, so finiteness alone is not integer validation.

predicate.name: predicate
predicate.definition: A function that returns true or false to answer a condition about the input it receives.

argument.name: argument
argument.definition: A value supplied when calling a function. An omitted argument is undefined unless the function supplies a default; a function does not automatically read a similarly named local value from its caller.
examples: Number.isInteger(3) // 3 is the argument supplied to this call

truthiness.name: truthiness
truthiness.definition: How JavaScript treats a value in a condition. null acts as false, while an object acts as true.

module-export.name: module export
module-export.definition: A value that a file makes available so another file can import and use it.
